a.aria-label: UniProtKB:P54745 — catalyzes → RHEA:33308; MngA is one 658-residue EIIABC chain. MC4100 mngA deletion loses MG transport and pACS31 restores it; inverted membranes plus general PTS extracts and PEP form MG-P. This is not a purified three-protein reconstitution. Separate intact-cell uptake comparisons in MG-induced MC4100 reported weak reduction with glucose, mannose and mannitol, a smaller effect with trehalose, and no observed reduction with fructose, maltose, arabinose, gluconate, glycerate, 1-alpha-glucosylglycerol, 2-alpha-glucosylglycerate or 2-alpha-mannosylglycerol. The Discussion instead describes mannose and those three glycosyl analogues as not significantly inhibitory even at 1 mM against 0.1 micromolar radiolabeled MG; the mannose weak-effect/no-significant-effect tension remains unresolved. These are uptake comparisons, not direct binding, a proven competitive mechanism or inhibition constants. Separately, 300 mM NaCl during growth did not induce transport and reduced MG-dependent induction by about 50%; this is an induction endpoint, distinct from the KM522 500 mM salt-protection experiment and from a direct catalytic salt effect. None of these whole-cell comparisons is attributed to the pACS31 inverted-membrane assay.; Evidence: EcoCyc:ENZRXN0-3541, PMID:14645248, UniProtKB:P54745, PMID:14645248, PMID:14645248, PMID:14645248, PMID:14645248

a.aria-label: UniProtKB:P37047 — activates → Entrez:947632; subject experimental construct: MC4100 reporter/loss-rescue context: active wild-type or pRM1-complemented SdaR/CdaR is inferred from loss in JA176 (paper-numbered P297S) and JA177 (Tn5 20 nt before stop); these mutants are not active endpoints. (XPath /html/body/div[2]/div[2]/div/div[1]/div/div[2]/main/article/section[2]/section/section[5]/p[2]); Evidence PMID:10762278: MC4100 sdaR-promoter-lacZ reporters respond to the three inducing carbon sources only with functional SdaR. (XPath /html/body/div[2]/div[2]/div/div[1]/div/div[2]/main/article/section[2]/section/section[3]/section[1]/figure/figcaption/p; paragraph containing 'TmaR forms clusters that localize'); Evidence PMID:33376208: Figure2 specifies TmaR-YFP, EI-mCherry and plasmid His-TmaR in Far-Western assays, with His-only and mCherry controls. (XPath /html/body/div[2]/div[2]/div/div[1]/div/div[2]/main/article/section[2]/section/section[3]/section[2]/figure/figcaption/p; paragraph containing 'TmaR and EI exhibit colocalization'); object experimental construct: Fluorescently tagged EI and Tyr122 variants in localization experiments. Tyr122-dependent polar recruitment is distinct from catalytic His189 phosphorylation.; Evidence UniProtKB:P08839: EI polar recruitment depends on Tyr122 and TmaR, based on the cited spatial-regulation study. (comments[commentType=SUBCELLULAR LOCATION]); Evidence PMID:33376208: The localization experiment compares EI-mCherry with EIY122F-mCherry; this is distinct from His189 catalytic phosphorylation. (XPath /html/body/div[2]/div[2]/div/div[1]/div/div[2]/main/article/section[2]/section/section[3]/section[6]/p[1]; paragraph containing 'To examine whether Tyr122 is important'); TmaR controls PtsI localization and activity by polar sequestration/release in general sugar studies. Tagged WT and phosphosite-mutant constructs establish context; no MG-specific control, universal occupancy or fixed TmaR–EI stoichiometry is asserted.; Evidence: PMID:33376208

a.aria-label: Carbohydrate diacid regulator; UniProtKB:P37047; Declared type: protein; experimental construct: MC4100 reporter/loss-rescue context: active wild-type or pRM1-complemented SdaR/CdaR is inferred from loss in JA176 (paper-numbered P297S) and JA177 (Tn5 20 nt before stop); these mutants are not active endpoints. The paper uses a 391-aa reference versus current P37047 (385 aa); residue numbering is not mapped to the current chain.; Evidence PMID:10762278: The paper reports a 391-residue yaeG/sdaR reference, JA176 Pro297-to-Ser substitution and JA177 Tn5 insertion 20 nucleotides before the stop codon. These loss mutants inform regulator assignment. (XPath /html/body/div[2]/div[2]/div/div[1]/div/div[2]/main/article/section[2]/section/section[5]/p[1]); Evidence PMID:10762278: pRM1 contains MC4100 sdaR amplified and cloned in pBluescript; it restores JA176/JA177 growth on glucarate, galactarate and glycerate. Loss and rescue support an activator role, not activation by mutant proteins. (XPath /html/body/div[2]/div[2]/div/div[1]/div/div[2]/main/article/section[2]/section/section[5]/p[2]); Evidence PMID:10762278: MC4100 sdaR-promoter-lacZ reporters respond to the three inducing carbon sources only with functional SdaR. The source interprets loss of sdaR-lacZ and garP-lacZ activation in knockouts as positive control. (XPath /html/body/div[2]/div[2]/div/div[1]/div/div[2]/main/article/section[2]/section/section[6]/p[1] | /html/body/div[2]/div[2]/div/div[1]/div/div[2]/main/article/section[2]/section/section[6]/p[2]); Evidence UniProtKB:P37047: The current issuing P37047 reference is 385 residues; its gene name is cdaR with sdaR and yaeG synonyms. This anchors identity, not equivalence to the paper’s 391-residue sequence numbering. (primaryAccession; sequence.length; genes)
